_about: The studio's path to every licence and terms page it relies on for AI-generated content: the page, the exact clause, its date, and R&D's verdict per use. Uses: assets (shipping output commercially), training (output as training data), evaluation (output in tests or controls), code (AI-written code in studio tools). Verdicts: proven, conditions (proven with the conditions listed), barred, not_proven, n/a. snapshot_sha256 is the sha256 of the page text as fetched on read_date; full-text snapshots are kept off the repo (see README). This is a reading of published terms, not legal advice.

TTS models from large providers
base_model:
yl4579/StyleTTS2-LJSpeech
conditions: Apache-2.0: shipping the weights carries the licence text and any NOTICE; synthesized speech is not claimed by the licence

Kokoro names StyleTTS2-LJSpeech as its base model, whose pre-trained-model terms ask that listeners be told the speech is synthesized unless the speakers gave permission (entry styletts2-pretrained-model-terms); a credit saying the voices are synthesized by Kokoro meets it
entries.notes: Read by R&D on 2026-10-22 for Escape the Valley 2.0's native voice, at the Editor's request; every clause re-read at the raw README. Provenance note, not a bar: the card says its training data includes synthetic audio from closed TTS providers' models, and CC BY audio (Koniwa CC BY 3.0, SIWIS CC BY 4.0) credited on the card. The studio agreed to none of those providers' terms and uses only Kokoro's outputs, so no clause the studio is bound by restricts the use; for the full-provenance aim the voice is not a clean-room asset.

covers: StyleTTS 2 pre-trained models (yl4579/StyleTTS2, including StyleTTS2-LJSpeech, Kokoro-82M's base model); the code is MIT
clauses: Code: MIT License

Before using these pre-trained models, you agree to inform the listeners that the speech samples are synthesized by the pre-trained models, unless you have the permission to use the voice you synthesize.
You only need to abide by the above rules if you use **the pre-trained models** and the voices are **NOT** in the training set
conditions: Synthesized speech made public is disclosed as synthesized (a credit is enough), unless the voice's speaker gave permission
R&D's reading, conservative: the terms bind StyleTTS 2's own pre-trained models; whether they carry into Kokoro's separately licensed weights is not stated, so the disclosure is kept
entries.notes: Read by R&D on 2026-10-22 while tracing Kokoro-82M's base model (the StyleTTS2-LJSpeech Hub repo has no card or licence tag). The HF repo yl4579/StyleTTS2-LJSpeech holds only the checkpoint and config.

covers: sherpa-onnx, the runtime that serves Kokoro-82M
clauses: Apache License
Version 2.0, January 2004
conditions: Apache-2.0: shipping the runtime carries the licence text and any NOTICE

Corrected 2026-10-22 (the Editor's check, re-read by R&D): no release drops espeak-ng (GPL-3.0). The latest release, v1.13.8 (crates.io and GitHub), includes espeak-ng-for-piper and piper-phonemize in CMakeLists.txt whenever TTS is built, and sherpa-onnx-static.pc.in links -lespeak-ng, so any TTS build of a released version links GPL code even if only the lexicon path runs. Only master's Kokoro config says espeak-ng is ignored from v2.0.0, which is unreleased
So a game binary may use sherpa-onnx TTS only from a pinned master commit whose build is shown to link no espeak-ng or piper_phonemize symbols or libraries; otherwise not
The lexicon files shipped with sherpa-onnx's Kokoro packages were not read; check their licence before bundling them
entries.notes: Read by R&D on 2026-10-22 for Escape the Valley 2.0's native voice, at the Editor's request.
